newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks OSCE role in Yugoslav reforms.
newsitem.headline: France seeks OSCE role in Yugoslav reforms.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette urged Yugoslavia on Monday to accept international mediation in its electoral reform process, saying it might hasten the country's return to a pan-European security forum.

"I suggested that...the OSCE be asked to organise a political dialogue between the the government and the political parties," de Charette told reporters after a lunch with Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic.

"I know that Yugoslavia is not a member of the OSCE and that it wants to be one. I have no doubt that if these proposals were adopted by the Yugoslav authorities, it would be an element weighing heavily in that direction," de Charette said.

He said the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) should be asked to recommend reforms in election laws, political expression in Yugoslav media, party financing and the electoral calendar.
Milutinovic called his talks with de Charette "profound" and said he would pass on the proposals to his government and give them serious consideration.

After weeks of protests against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's annulment of local election results, Belgrade allowed an OSCE mission to visit the country and eventually accepted its recommendation to restore opposition victories.

De Charette renewed a European Union request to open an office in Pristina, the capital of Serbia's troubled Kosovo province, where ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs by about nine to one. Kosovo has been seeking greater autonomy from Belgrade.

De Charette asked Yugoslavia to delay ratification of an accord on mutual recognition with the Bosnian Serb republic until the international community's High Representative for Bosnia, Carl Bildt, confirmed that the agreement conformed with the Dayton Accords ending the Bosnian war.
